title: Causal-Adapter: Taming Text-to-Image Diffusion for Faithful Counterfactual Generation
claim: Editing only the target attribute leaves dependent attributes inconsistent; following the causal graph propagates interventions to dependents and gives coherent counterfactuals.
layout: 2 panels: causal graph left, 3x3 face grid right, colored arrows
description: The left panel is a causal graph for CelebA. Colored circular nodes are age (a, pink), gender (g, blue), beard (br, yellow), bald (bl, green) and image (x, gray). Black arrows run from a and g to br and bl, and from all four to x. A legend below defines the symbols. The right panel is a 3x3 grid of face photos. The columns are Image, Non-Causal and Causal. The rows are the interventions do(a=1) Old to Young, do(a=0) Young to Old, and do(g=1) Female to Male. Pastel arrows on the faces match the node colors. They mark the intervened attribute and the dependents that changed or failed to change. The Non-Causal column changes only the target attribute. The Causal column also changes beard and baldness. The eye goes first to the graph and then to the contrast between the last two columns.
caption: Non-causal editing modifies only the target attribute (e.g. age, gender); causal editing propagates changes to related attributes (e.g. beard, baldness) enforced by the causal graph.
abstract: We present Causal-Adapter, a modular framework that adapts frozen text-to-image diffusion backbones for counterfactual image generation. Our method supports causal interventions on target attributes and consistently propagates their effects to causal dependents while preserving the core identity of the image. Unlike prior approaches that rely on prompt engineering without explicit causal structure, Causal-Adapter leverages structural causal modeling with two attribute-regularization strategies: (i) prompt-aligned injection, which aligns causal attributes with textual embeddings for precise semantic control, and (ii) a conditioned token contrastive loss that disentangles attribute factors and reduces spurious correlations. Causal-Adapter achieves state-of-the-art performance on both synthetic and real-world datasets, including up to a 91% reduction in MAE on Pendulum for accurate attribute control and up to an 87% reduction in FID on ADNI for high-fidelity MRI generation. These results demonstrate robust, generalizable counterfactual editing with faithful attribute modification and strong identity preservation. Code and models will be released at: https://leitong02.github.io/causaladapter/.
